assessments.reasoning: Section 5.3.1.5 puts an optional mechanism in each ordinary positional or optional parameter form. Page 66 makes omission equivalent to an explicitly written ByRef mechanism.

challenge.method: Read the positional and optional productions on p.65, the default rule on p.66, and the apparently overlapping runtime bullets on p.67. Try applying the rule to a Property Let or Set value parameter on p.68, then cross-check invocation on p.72.
challenge.results: Both p.67 runtime bullets print ByVal for different positional behavior and cannot be used to derive aliasing here. Page 68 gives the setter value parameter a distinct ByVal rule. The explicit static equivalence on p.66 controls the ordinary positional and optional cases and survives these boundaries.

limitations: This judgment applies to the exact May 20, 2025 MS-VBAL revision 2.4. The publisher currently lists a later edition. Its requirements and behavior of any Office host are outside this review.
This supports static parameter-notation equivalence. It supplies no aliasing conclusion or default for a setter assignment value parameter.
